requirements.statement: The application displays a sign-in page matching the supplied wireframe's visible content.
acceptance_criteria: Given a visitor opens the sign-in page, when the page renders, then a narrow bordered panel on a white background contains the “Sign in” heading, a labeled “Email address” input with “name@example.com” placeholder, and a labeled “Password” input.
Given the sign-in page is displayed, when a visitor enters a password, then its characters are masked.

Given a visitor opens the sign-in page, when the page renders, then a blue underlined “Forgot password?” link, a dark wide “Sign in” button, and a gray “No account? Contact your administrator.” footer appear as pictured.

requirements.statement: The sign-in page's “Forgot password?” link starts a password-reset request flow.
acceptance_criteria: Given the sign-in page is displayed, when a visitor follows “Forgot password?”, then the visitor can submit a reset request for an account identifier.

requirements.statement: The application responds identically to password-reset requests for existing and nonexistent accounts.
acceptance_criteria: Given equivalent reset requests for a synthetic account identifier and an unknown identifier, when each is submitted under the same conditions, then the visitor-facing responses are identical and do not disclose which account exists.

requirements.statement: The application limits password-reset requests to five per account per hour.
acceptance_criteria: Given five reset requests for the same synthetic account within one hour, when a sixth request is submitted within that hour, then no sixth reset link is issued for that account.
Given that account's applicable one-hour request period has elapsed, when another reset request is submitted, then the prior period's five requests do not prevent a new eligible request.

requirements.statement: An accepted password-reset request for a synthetic account makes a reset link available through the in-memory notification sink.
acceptance_criteria: Given a synthetic account and an eligible reset request, when the request is submitted, then the sink records a reset link for that account.
Given a nonexistent account identifier, when a reset request is submitted, then no account-specific reset link is recorded.

requirements.statement: A password-reset link can complete at most one password reset.
acceptance_criteria: Given an unexpired reset link, when a reset is completed with it and the same link is submitted again, then the later submission cannot complete another reset.

requirements.statement: A password-reset link issued at time t expires 30 minutes after issuance, at t+30 minutes.
acceptance_criteria: Given a reset link issued at time t, when a reset is attempted strictly before t+30 minutes, then the link remains eligible if otherwise valid and unused.
Given a reset link issued at time t, when a reset is attempted at or after t+30 minutes, then the link must not complete a reset.

requirements.statement: Completing a valid password reset replaces the account's password with the submitted new password.
acceptance_criteria: Given a synthetic account and a valid unused link, when a new password is submitted through the reset flow, then the account accepts the new password and no longer accepts the previous password.

requirements.statement: Completing a password reset signs the account out of every active session.
acceptance_criteria: Given a synthetic account with multiple active sessions, when its password is successfully reset, then none of those sessions remains authenticated for that account.

requirements.statement: Every successful password reset produces a notification addressed to the account owner in the in-memory notification sink.
acceptance_criteria: Given a synthetic account, when its password is successfully reset, then the sink records an owner-addressed successful-reset notification for that reset.

requirements.statement: The prototype performs account-recovery behavior using synthetic accounts.
acceptance_criteria: Given the application is configured for testing, when the recovery flow is exercised, then the participating accounts are synthetic rather than real user accounts.

requirements.statement: The prototype records recovery notifications in an in-memory sink rather than delivering them through an external service.
acceptance_criteria: Given a recovery link or successful-reset notification is generated, when its delivery is inspected, then a record is available in the in-memory sink without requiring an external delivery service.
Given a Python 3.12 environment with the declared dependencies installed, when the application and tests are started, then they execute under that interpreter.

requirements.statement: The password-reset application uses Flask to handle its web requests.
acceptance_criteria: Given the application is running, when a visitor requests its sign-in and recovery routes, then Flask handles those requests.

requirements.statement: The application's sign-in and recovery pages are rendered on the server.
acceptance_criteria: Given a visitor requests a sign-in or recovery page, when the response is received, then its page content is present in the server response without requiring client-side rendering.

requirements.statement: The project provides automated pytest tests for the password-reset application's required behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Given Python 3.12 and the declared test dependencies, when pytest runs, then automated tests exercise the pictured sign-in entry point, non-enumerating response, per-account request limit, link issuance, single use, expiration, password replacement, all-session sign-out, and owner notification.

requirements.statement: The project documents the prototype's production limitations.
acceptance_criteria: Given a reader opens the project documentation, when the production-limitations section is read, then it identifies synthetic accounts and the in-memory notification sink as unsuitable substitutes for production account and delivery systems.

requirements.statement: The project remains undeployed and does not include a deployment workflow.
acceptance_criteria: Given the delivered project, when its changes and workflow files are inspected, then no deployment action was performed and no deployment workflow was added.
